title: Zephyr Retail - Embedding latency & econ pilot discovery
summary: Discovery focused on embedding dimensionality, vector DB integration, and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a rerank/ hybrid search pilot. Zephyr needs predictable p99 latency (~100-150ms target for rerank path), cost sensitivity at scale (~100M+ docs), and compliance (SOC2 + customer-managed KMS). Agreed next steps: SE to run a small benchmarks spreadsheet, AE to share pricing and security pack, schedule pilot kickoff week of Dec 6.
topics: current retrieval stack and pain points
hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
rerank flow and top-K fanout economics

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-11-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dana Liu (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SA), Priya Menon (Zephyr Head of Search), Tom Aguilar (Zephyr Platform Eng), Lena Novak (Zephyr CTO), Rajiv Sen (Zephyr Data Eng)

Auto-summary: quick discovery to understand Zephyr's retrieval stack, p99 latency targets, embedding dims, and to scope a pilot focusing on rerank after vector DB retrieval.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, and with me is Dana and Carlos. How's it going?
[00:12] Priya: Hi Samir, doing well. Thanks for fitting us in, we wanted to go over embedding strategy and hosting options.
[00:22] Dana: Quick agenda - understand current infra, QPS and docs, talk about embed dims and rerank flow, then map hosting options to requirements.
[00:30] Tom: Sounds good. For context, Zephyr runs search for our retail catalog and help center, roughly 120 QPS peak across a mixed set of queries, about 150M documents but only ~20M are active product rows.
[00:45] Samir: That's helpful. When you say rerank, are you doing vector search top-K then a separate neural rerank?
[00:50] Priya: Yes - we currently generate embeddings in-house with an open model, then Faiss does nearest neighbors fetch, take top 50, then we run a reranker to get better relevance - latency's been the pain point.
[01:05] Dana: And do you push reranking to a model endpoint or is it batch? Is the rerank run synchronously in the request path?
[01:12] Priya: Synchronous, which is why p99 is spiky. Our target would be around 100-150ms for rerank path p99 if possible.
[01:20] Carlos: Ok. Quick clarifying question: what's your embedding dimension today and which model?
[01:25] Rajiv: We're on a 1536-d float32 embedding from a hosted open model - size is big and storage/ops are expensive. We're exploring 768 dims or compact embeddings to reduce costs.
[01:35] Samir: That matches what we see. Dims trade off recall vs storage/throughput. For your scale, 768 is often a sweet spot, or quantized 1536/128 using int8/4-bit for vector DBs.
[01:49] Tom: How does Redwood integrate with Faiss or Milvus? We have an existing Faiss setup on k8s and would prefer minimal changes.
[01:56] Dana: Redwood doesn't force a particular vector DB. Common patterns: 1) Run embedding in your pipeline, store in Faiss/Milvus/PineCone, then call search -> fetch topK ids -> call Redwood for rerank via a single request passing candidate texts & queries. 2) Alternatively Redwood can host embedding generation and return vectors to be stored in your DB. So you can keep Faiss as-is.
[02:18] Priya: Interesting. For the rerank call, what's typical latency if we send topK=50 to Redwood hosted?
[02:24] Carlos: For a single request to a light reranker model optimized on GPU, you can see 30-80ms depending on model size and token lengths. But the full path includes vector DB fetch time and network. So your overall p99 depends on the slowest leg.
[02:40] Rajiv: Our Faiss knn is around 20-30ms p95 currently. Combined we hit 220-300ms p99 which is above target.
[02:50] Dana: There are a few levers: reduce topK, use a smaller rerank model, run rerank on Dedicated instances to get more predictable tail latency, and enable prefix/KV caching for repeated queries.
[03:05] Priya: Can you explain the KV cache bit? I thought KV cache was for autoregressive generation.
[03:10] Dana: Good point - sorry that was sloppy. For generation KV cache helps for long contexts. For rerank we use request caching - if queries are repeated we can cache candidate embeddings or rerank scores. Also we have footprint-level caching on top of continuous batching to improve throughput.
[03:28] Tom: Continuous batching - does that add latency? We need tight latency SLOs.
[03:33] Carlos: Continuous batching tries to pack requests to improve GPU utilization while respecting max latency windows. You can set latency SLOs and batching will respect that up to the configured window; below that you get better cost/throughput without increasing p99 too much.
[03:48] Lena: If we consider Dedicated, what does that mean operationally? Do you manage the GPUs or we do?
[03:53] Samir: Redwood Dedicated = reserved GPU pools owned by Redwood but isolated to your account. We manage runtime and orchestration; you get predictable capacity and dedicated routing. Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) gives you more network isolation and customer-managed control plane, but operational split is different and there's more work for infra.
[04:12] Priya: Compliance is big - SOC2 + customer KMS for keys. Would private be required for KMS?
[04:18] Dana: Not necessarily. For Hosted we support BYOK via cloud KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) and we provide audit logs. Private gives maximal isolation. We'll include the detailed security notes in the pack.
[04:31] Rajiv: One other thing: our vector DB is sharded across three clusters for geo-failover. Any gotchas with fanout when you do rerank?
[04:40] Carlos: Fanout increases cost linearly because if you query multiple shards you'll get more candidates to rerank. Strategies: run initial scoring in DB and only rerank a narrow topK from each shard, or do a fast approximate global topK with PQ/IVF then rerank. We'll help design shard-aware fanout to meet your cost/latency targets.
[04:58] Tom: Can you give an order-of-magnitude on cost per 1M rerank calls on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[05:05] Samir: We'll send concrete pricing, but general guidance: Hosted is simplest but marginal cost per call is higher. Dedicated amortizes GPU cost over your throughput so per-call cost drops significantly at scale, especially with batching and quantized models. Private has licensing/cohort costs but gives predictable unit economics. I'll put numbers in the pricing sheet.
[05:26] Priya: For embedding dims - if we drop to 768, how much recall loss do you usually see?
[05:31] Dana: It's workload dependent. For product-title and short descriptions 768 often retains 95% of recall for nearest-neighbor search vs 1536; but you should run an eval. Part of the pilot would be an embedding A/B where we compute recall and rerank lift.
[05:48] Rajiv: We also want to explore quantized embeddings on disk (8-bit or 4-bit). Any limitations with Faiss?
[05:54] Dana: Faiss supports various compressed indexes (PQ, OPQ, IVF) and int8 quantization patterns. Milvus/others also have their own. Redwood's runtime accepts compact/quantized vectors; we just need to confirm serialization formats.
[06:08] Tom: Are there examples where teams keep embed generation in-house but use Redwood for rerank only?
[06:14] Samir: Yes that's common. Keeps you in control of embeddings and indexing, while Redwood provides the low-latency reranker and optional hosted embeddings later.
[06:24] Priya: Any recommended rerank model sizes? We're sensitive to latency but want relevance.
[06:29] Carlos: For rerank, tiny cross-encoders or distilled models strike a good balance. In our benchmarks, a distilled reranker can do topK=50 rerank in ~45ms median on a mid-tier GPU. If you need <100ms p99, dedicated instances with reserved capacity are recommended.
[06:46] Rajiv: What about cold-starts and warm caches? We see big spikes during campaign launches.
[06:51] Dana: Warm-up strategies: preload embeddings for expected hot queries, use prefix caching for popular queries, and run lightweight warm-up traffic. Dedicated with burst policies can also help handle campaign spikes.
[07:06] Tom: For the pilot, what's a reasonable sample size? We can provide an anonymized 10k doc set and 2k queries.
[07:12] Samir: That's ideal for smoke tests. For more representative numbers, 100k docs helps, but to start 10k + 2k queries is good. We'll run baseline on Hosted and a small Dedicated config.
[07:23] Priya: Questions about network - our infra sits in AWS eu-west-1, can Redwood route to that region?
[07:29] Samir: Yes, we have regions in AWS eu-west-1 and can deploy Dedicated capacity there. Private VPC peering is also supported for Private deployments.
[07:38] Rajiv: Any limitations on batch sizes or token limits for rerank?
[07:42] Dana: Rerank is mostly constrained by sequence length: candidate text length plus query length. We typically truncate to meaningful windows. For batching, there's a soft max request size - we'll share specifics in the benchmark template.
[07:57] Lena: I wanted to flag business priorities: cost savings in 6 months and predictable latency for conversion-sensitive queries. If you can show a 20-30% unit cost reduction with same/better relevance, we're interested in Dedicated.
[08:12] Samir: That's a clear goal. We'll design pilot success criteria: 1) p99 rerank path under 150ms, 2) equal or better relevance metrics on your eval set, 3) demonstrable cost per query improvement within 8-12 weeks.
[08:27] Priya: Are there any redwood-specific SDKs for rerank calls and request shaping?
[08:32] Dana: Yes, SDKs (python/node) support bundled candidate rerank calls - you supply query and candidate payloads. There's also streaming support for generation flows. We'll share code snippets in the follow-up.
[08:45] Tom: About data retention - we need 90-day retention and deletion on demand.
[08:50] Dana: Hosted supports configurable retention and deletion APIs; Private gives you full control, but hosted can meet 90-day and deletion SLAs. We'll include the policy docs.
[08:59] Rajiv: A question on routing: can we route high-value traffic to Dedicated and lower-tier to Hosted to save costs?
[09:05] Carlos: Yes, Redwood supports smart routing policies by traffic tag, user cohort, or latency requirements. You can map conversion-critical routes to Dedicated and others to hosted or cheaper quantized variants.
[09:20] Priya: That could work well for us.
[09:23] Samir: Let's talk pilot plan and timeline - pilot scope, endpoints, metrics.
[09:28] Dana: Proposed pilot: Week 0 - onboarding + dataset exchange; Week 1 - baseline runs (Hosted and local rerank baseline), Week 2 - Dedicated smoke test, Week 3 - tuned reranking + metrics evaluation. Aim to have measurable delta by end of Week 3 or 4.
[09:47] Tom: Who will own the test infra for Faiss? We will provide a k8s namespace and credentials.
[09:53] Samir: Perfect. Dana will provide instructions for connector and request format, Carlos will assist on sharding and fanout config.
[10:02] Priya: Any quick wins to reduce token sizes for rerank?
[10:06] Dana: Truncate to product title + nearest sentence rather than full description, remove HTML/boilerplate; sometimes a 30-50% token shrink gives big latency wins with negligible recall loss.
[10:18] Rajiv: Ok makes sense.
[10:20] Samir: I'll recap before we close. Action items: pricing/security pack to Zephyr, Redwood SE to run baseline tests and share spreadsheet, Zephyr to provide datasets and credentials. Proposal to kick off week of Dec 6.
[10:35] Lena: That timeline works. Anything else?
[10:40] Priya: Competitors question - we use Pinecone for one non-critical service; how do you compare?
[10:44] Samir: Pinecone is a great managed vector DB; our focus is inference/rerank and unified routing. Many customers use Pinecone for storage + Redwood for rerank. We'll include a short comparison note.
[10:56] Tom: Ok thanks - maybe include Milvus notes as well since we might test both.
[11:00] Dana: Will do.
[11:03] Samir: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[11:08] Priya: Thanks, bye.

--- End transcript ---
